title: Driver per-unit candidate result v1
description: One completed sub-unit of a driver stage: the receipt fields that decide whether it may be reused, plus the validated provider result itself. A stage-level receipt records that a whole stage finished; this records that ONE document or bundle finished, so an interruption reruns only the unfinished unit. The payload is stored because a resume must not re-call the provider merely to recover a result the driver already validated. DAO-owned: issued only by write-driver-candidate, never through write-contract, so a driver cannot forge a completed unit for itself.

unit_id.description: The parent stage unit this candidate belongs to (for example checkpoint_1).

candidate_id.description: Identifies the sub-unit within the stage unit: one document for claim-analysis checkpoint 1, one insurer bundle for denial-response initial extraction.

input_digests.description: Only the digests this ONE unit consumed. Scoping matters: a stage-wide digest set would invalidate every unit when any document's redacted text changes, which is exactly the over-invalidation this file exists to prevent.

status.description: Only a completed, driver-validated unit is persisted. An interrupted unit leaves no candidate file at all, which is what makes its absence the resume signal.

result.description: The provider output for this unit, after the driver's own validation passed. Reused verbatim on resume.

call_usage.description: Provider-reported token counts, one entry per provider call (a run that needed P4's correction records both). Copied verbatim from the provider's own usage report, never derived -- a count this harness computed would be indistinguishable from one the provider measured. Diagnostic only: deliberately outside input_fingerprint, so recording it never changes whether a candidate can be reused.
